rationale: C++ has a genuinely low ceiling and this floor is deliberately not near 1.0. tree-sitter has no preprocessor, so every unexpandable macro is a token the grammar must guess at, and fmt is macro-dense (FMT_BEGIN_NAMESPACE, FMT_CONSTEXPR, FMT_API, gtest's TEST). 41 of the full repo's 72 files contain ERROR nodes. Almost every uncaptured named function here is stranded behind a compound_statement or ERROR in its ancestor chain — the enclosing namespace or class failed to parse and collapsed into a bare block, so the function survives but its scope does not. Emitting entities for them was rejected: the name is recoverable but the qualified name is not, and a Callable with a wrong qn resolves to the wrong target rather than to nothing. Their calls are still recovered, because _extract_calls descends into that debris and attributes to the nearest scope that did survive (ADR-0031) — which is why calls sits at 0.965 while named_funcs sits at 0.71. Measured on the full 72-file checkout the same walker scores named_funcs 0.641 / calls 0.971 / duplicate_uids 304; this fixture reads higher on named_funcs only because fmt's four giant headers (base.h, format.h, chrono.h, format-inl.h — 418KB, scoring 0.50-0.70) dominate the repo by weight and cannot be vendored within the size budget. The 3.5% call shortfall is 258 C++ named casts (static_cast/reinterpret_cast/const_cast/dynamic_cast), which the grammar shapes exactly like calls but which are keywords, not callables — an edge to one could never resolve; the rest is calls with no static callee name at all (fp[i](), (*fp)(), chained f()()). named_funcs is 0.01 LOWER than the 0.72 first recorded here, and deliberately so: three macro invocations that the grammar reports as function definitions (FMT_CATCH, gtest's GTEST_LOCK_EXCLUDED_) stopped emitting entities. The measurement counts them as named forms because it can only see the node type, so suppressing a confidently-wrong node is scored as a coverage loss. The 11 remaining colliding uids are NOT fixable from this walker: they are genuine C++ overloads and constructors (file::dup2 with and without an error_code, two SFINAE test_value overloads, copy and move constructors, operator() overloads) plus two #ifdef arms of convert_rwcount that really are two definitions of one name. Separating those needs the signature in the uid, which is a cross-cutting schema change. One of the 11 — scan.detail — is a namespace mis-parsed as a function, the same debris class described above. NOTE for whoever reads this next: the single largest cause of the low named_funcs is NOT macros. .h is registered to the C grammar (_C_EXTENSIONS in parsing/languages/cpp.py) but fmt's headers are C++, so 23 of 25 fail to parse; under the C++ grammar the same headers yield 2968 function_definition nodes instead of 1454. Re-routing .h lifts the repo to named_funcs 0.710 with 3531 Callables instead of 2229 and drops module-scope calls from 15.5% to 2.2%. That was left alone deliberately — it changes how every existing C project's headers are labelled and there was no C corpus here to prove it is not a regression.
